chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to Ibn Ḥazm that he should send to him the charity endowment of ʿAlī, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān. Ibn Ḥazm then sent to Zayd ibn al-Ḥasan, and he was the eldest of them, and asked him about the charity. So Zayd said: The guardian after ʿAlī was al-Ḥasan, and after al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and after al-Ḥusayn, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and after ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī; so send to him.
So Ibn Ḥazm sent to my father, and my father sent me with the letter to him, until I delivered it to Ibn Ḥazm.

Then some of us said to him: Do the sons of al-Ḥasan recognize this? He said: Yes, just as they recognize that this is night, but envy drives them. If they had sought the truth by the truth, it would have been better for them, but they seek the world.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life or worldly gain sought in place of the truth
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةَ: the charity endowment or charitable property being requested and administered
key_terms.الْحَسَدُ: envy, described as the motive preventing acceptance of the truth
key_terms.الْحَسَنَ: Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, named as the first successor after Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in this report
key_terms.الْحَقَّ: the truth that ought to be sought and acknowledged
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنَ: Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, named as the next successor in the line of authority
key_terms.الْوَالِيَ: the rightful guardian or holder of authority in succession
key_terms.مُحَمَّدَ بْنَ عَلِيٍّ: Imam Muḥammad al-Bāqir عليه السلام, identified here as the authority to whom one should refer

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the succession of authority among the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام after Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration recounts a historical episode concerning the administration of charity endowments and identifies the rightful succession of authority after Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام through Imam al-Ḥasan, Imam al-Ḥusayn, Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and Imam Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليهما السلام. It also states that some people recognized this truth but were diverted by envy and worldly motives.
